marks.gloss_en: הוא דאמר כי האי תנא, דתניא: עקוד -- עקידת יד ורגל או שתי ידים ושתי רגלים (kind tanya_kevatei: no kind names a bare דתניא)
מיתיבי: עקוד -- שתי ידים ושתי רגלים -- the baraita's akud is not Rav Yehuda's foreleg-and-hind-leg
the baraita: akud is [binding] two forelegs and two hind legs
כי האי תנא: עקוד -- עקידת יד ורגל כיצחק בן אברהם -- the tanna's definition is Rav Yehuda's word for word (kind tanya_kevatei: the citation has no marker of its own)

אלא הוא דאמר כי האי תנא: עקוד -- עקידת יד ורגל כיצחק בן אברהם -- Rav Yehuda follows another tanna (= p_ry_kitanna_kyitzchak). The stam's first answer at 54a.13 (= p_ry_kitanna_o) was felled at 54a.14 and is recorded there, not here.
the baraita: akud is the binding of a foreleg and a hind leg, like Isaac son of Abraham

ואכתי לא דמי: בשלמא רישא וסיפא ניחא, מציעתא קשיא -- the first clause (foreleg and hind leg) and the last (ragul) match Rav Yehuda, but the middle clause (two and two) still does not; unanswered -- the stam turns with אלא
the mishna: a camel may not go out akud
Rav Yehuda: akud is the binding of a foreleg and a hind leg, like Isaac son of Abraham
one may not tie camels to one another and pull
ואמרי אינשי: ארעא מכבלתא דלא עבדא פירי -- common speech calls land that bears no fruit 'bound'
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: it was a land of chomton
אי הכי, היינו דכתיב ולא ישרו בעיניו -- מפני שמכובלין בכסף ובזהב לא ישרו בעיניו? -- if so, because they were bound up in silver and gold they were not right in his eyes?
אמר ליה: אין, כיון דעתירי ומפנקי לא עבדי עבידתא -- yes: being rich and pampered, they do not do work (= p_atirei_umefankei)
Rav Huna: [it is called the land of Kavul] because there were people in it bound up (mechubalin) in silver and gold
Rav: the halakha follows R' Yehuda
Rav: [goats bound] to dry is permitted
the baraita: goats go out bound to dry
דכתיב ויקרא להן ארץ כבול -- the verse names [poor] land 'kavul'
מאי משמע דהאי כבול לישנא דלא עביד פירי הוא -- the stam grounds its reading of kevulot in the word's sense of not bearing fruit
ewes may go out [on Shabbat] kevulot
כדתנן: שאת כצמר לבן -- the mishna whose 'white wool' carries the term (kind tanya_kevatei: no kind names a bare כדתנן)
the same כדתנן citation, through its explication: Rav Beivai bar Abaye's 'wool ... that is wrapped (מכבנין) for meilat' shows what מכבנין means
what are kevunot? [ewes] that are wrapped (mechabnin) for meilat
והתנן: אדם מותר עם כולם לחרוש ולמשוך -- a person is permitted to plow and pull with any animal, so there is no kilayim of a person
Rav Ashi: they taught [this] only with regard to kilayim
והתניא: התוכף תכיפה אחת אינה חיבור -- a single stitch is not a connection, so how could wrapping ropes make kilayim?
rather, the kilayim is that of ropes
לעולם כלאים דחבלים, והכי קאמר: ובלבד שלא יכרוך ויקשור (= p_yichroch_veyikshor)
and thus it [the mishna] says: provided he does not wrap and tie
והא תנא דבי שמואל טפחיים -- but the tanna of Shmuel's own school taught two handbreadths
Shmuel: provided the rope does not come out a handbreadth from beneath his hand
שמואל הלכה למעשה אתא לאשמועינן (= p_abaye_halakha_lemaase)
Abaye: now that Shmuel said one handbreadth and the tanna of his school two, Shmuel came to teach us the practical halakha
[the stam: what is the reason?] Rav Ashi: because he looks like one going to the chinga [market]
a camel may not go out with a saddlecloth tied to its tail
